clue.text: Servant with first husband at the front

indicators.note: says the husband's letter comes before everything else in the answer

parts.note: with means and, joining things together
a maiden voyage or speech is the first one

explanation.surface: A household servant, with the man of the house given precedence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like an ordinal, but it is MAIDEN, as in a maiden voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaiden is a female personal attendant, a servant in older usage.

clue.text: Husky in frost leading empty sledge

indicators.note: the frost word goes in front of the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: hoar is a white frost on grass and branches

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters, its contents removed

explanation.surface: A husky dog out in the frost pulls an unladen sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' reads as the sled dog, but it is the adjective for a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is a hoarse one: both mean rough and throaty, synonyms.

clue.text: New, a shocking pink serviette

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shocking suggests letters thrown into disorder, signalling a rearrangement of the colour word

explanation.surface: A new serviette in a garish, shocking-pink shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking pink' is a real colour, which hides that 'shocking' rearranges PINK into PKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviette is the British word for a table napkin, so the two are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Scoff awkward to rustle up for a first course, perhaps

parts.note: to scoff at is to mock

indicators.note: awkward suggests the following letters are clumsily arranged and need sorting

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that it is awkward to rustle up something to eat as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges TO RUSTLE UP into TURTLESOUP. 'Scoff' looks like eating greedily but means to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: This imitation turtle broth, made with calf's head, is served as a soup course, an example of a starter.

clue.text: Audience in Bury to contend with

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: A crowd in the Lancashire town of Bury has something to contend with.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town in north-west England, which disguises the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience with someone important is a formal meeting, a sense shared with a formal interview.

clue.text: Mistake made by troublesome child forgetting time

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out the time letter

parts.note: a little terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A naughty child makes a blunder and forgets the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake and an error are plain synonyms for something done wrong.

clue.text: Lived initially in large apartment

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for large

parts.note: fat means large or big

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone at first lived in a spacious apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat is the British term for an apartment, a self-contained set of rooms.

clue.text: Look to conceal terribly bitter text

indicators.note: concealing means holding something inside, so the look word wraps round the rest

parts.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means look

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the next word are badly mangled

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide a terribly bitter written passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes IBRETT from the bitter word; 'Look' is the old exclamation lo, as in lo and behold.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the words of an opera or musical, its written text.

clue.text: Brief delight, certainly, getting prize

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the delight word drops

parts.note: a treat is a delight or pleasure
sure, as a reply, means certainly

explanation.surface: A short-lived delight from certainly getting a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize' looks like a noun but is the verb, to value highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it dearly, the same verb sense as to cherish it.

clue.text: Dance show off

definitions.meaning: to perform a dance with flair and confidence

explanation.surface: A dance show is being cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show off' reads as a cancelled show, but it is the verb to flaunt oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both dancing with gusto and flaunting oneself proudly.

clue.text: Jelly and cream shortly after seeing that

indicators.note: the shortened cream word comes after the seeing-that word

parts.note: as can mean since or seeing that

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: the cream or pick of something is its best part

explanation.surface: A dessert of jelly and cream, served shortly after seeing that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' is not dairy but the best of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury meat jelly, a specific kind of the general term.

clue.text: Go and suggest what a DJ may use

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in a turn at a game
to table a motion is to put it forward or suggest it

explanation.surface: Take your turn and propose what a disc jockey might play.
explanation.definitionFit: Disc jockeys spin vinyl records on a rotating deck, so this is an example of their kit.

clue.text: Tot in American's brandy glass

definitions.meaning: in American usage, a balloon glass for brandy

explanation.surface: A small child in a wealthy American's brandy glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' suggests a toddler, but it is a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a small nip of liquor, and in the US also a balloon-shaped glass for cognac.

clue.text: News agency awfully sure about shortened name

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the rest
awfully suggests the letters are in a dreadful jumble
shortened cuts the final letter off the name word

parts.note: a term is a name or word for something

explanation.surface: A news agency is terribly certain about an abbreviated name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' gives REUS, which goes round TER; 'name' is a term, as in a term for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuters is an international wire service supplying stories to the media, a news agency.

clue.text: Instructs wizard in anorak

parts.note: to train is to instruct
Harry Potter is the boy wizard of the novels

explanation.surface: A boy wizard is being taught while wearing a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' seems the jacket, but in British slang an anorak is an obsessive hobbyist, the stereotype being a rail enthusiast noting engine numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway enthusiasts are the classic example of the British slang word for an obsessive geek.

clue.text: Had doubts about speed cuts working

indicators.note: working means the letters are being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was sceptical about cuts to speed limits being effective.
explanation.definitionFit: To have doubts about someone is to distrust them, a synonym of this verb.

clue.text: Hidden from view, old boy's pickled

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil, and the 's adds S
cured means preserved, as by pickling

explanation.surface: A former pupil, drunk, has vanished from sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' suggests drunk, but here it means preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concealed or covered over is out of sight, a synonym.

clue.text: Almost mandatory somehow, to show how lottery numbers are drawn?

indicators.note: somehow tells us the letters are put together in some new way
almost means not quite all of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A draw procedure that is nearly compulsory, explaining how lottery balls come out.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator after 'Almost' turns MANDATOR (the word less its Y) into the answer's letters; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lottery balls come out by chance, with no pattern, which is the meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Represented as foremost of lackeys — who better?

definitions.text: Represented as foremost of lackeys — who better?

indicators.note: represented, read as re-presented, means the letters are presented again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: foremost of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone described as the chief of the menial servants: who could be better suited?
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is AS, L (first of 'lackeys') and WHO BETTER, rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief bottle-washer is a jokey phrase for a dogsbody who does everything, the top drudge among menials.

clue.text: Jones the architect checking daughter's colour

indicators.note: checking means holding back or restraining, so the architect contains the daughter

parts.note: Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect
D abbreviates daughter, and the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An architect named Jones looks over his daughter's choice of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep blue-violet is one of the seven colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Parliamentary break in depression?

definitions.meaning: a period when parliament is not sitting
a hollow or alcove set back into a wall or surface

explanation.surface: Parliament's holiday falls during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests an economic or mental low, but it is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a holiday adjournment of a legislature and an indented niche.

clue.text: Cordial about head of human skeleton

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cordial goes round the picked letter

parts.note: cassis is a blackcurrant cordial or liqueur

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A friendly remark about the head of a human skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' reads as friendly but is the blackcurrant drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's chassis is its base frame, the skeleton on which the body is built.

clue.text: Dance in rehearsals again

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A dance is being practised once more in rehearsals.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a Latin American partner dance, an example of the category.

clue.text: Intrinsic feature of German city church

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A defining characteristic of a German city's church.
explanation.definitionFit: The core quality that makes something what it is, a synonym for an intrinsic nature.

clue.text: Radical hairstyle for swimmer?

parts.note: red means politically radical or left-wing
a mullet is the short-front, long-back haircut

explanation.surface: An extreme haircut suitable for someone going swimming?
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer?' is a fish, the question mark flagging a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: This prized Mediterranean food fish is an example of a swimming creature.

clue.text: Join one heading for Exeter

parts.note: a unit is a single one

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the city name is taken

explanation.surface: Join someone travelling towards Exeter, a city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together or combine, a synonym of the verb join.

clue.text: Silent animated Disney film, unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means losing the final letter

parts.note: Dumbo is the 1941 Disney cartoon about a flying elephant

explanation.surface: A Disney cartoon left incomplete, with no soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable or unwilling to speak means saying nothing, a synonym for mute.

clue.text: Fair's fare?

parts.note: the food sold at a funfair, with fair and fare sounding alike for the joke

explanation.surface: A pun on the rhyme of a funfair and the food on offer there.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun-sugar sweets on sticks are the classic snack sold at funfairs.
